description: Consolidated policy data for the extraction-slice safety nets: each rule set is read from this one record so no test file hard-codes policy that belongs to an ownership map. Read by tests/test_app_gui_patch_surface.py (the patch-surface net, whose load_* loaders validate every section), tests/test_payload_policy_ownership.py, tests/test_stem_cache_write_path.py (the writer-manifest net) and extraction-slice tooling that needs to know what has already been moved.

the_oracle.gui_render.note: Only the no-op-after-move name. The three class names must NOT be listed: MainWindow (still in app_gui) constructs RenderWorker, PreviewWorker and RenderProgressDialog from app_gui globals, so app_gui-level class patches remain live and legitimate.

the_oracle.gui_recording.note: Only the worker: MainWindow constructs it only via RecordingStudioDialog's body, which resolves the name from gui_recording's globals, so an app_gui-level patch is a silent no-op. RecordingStudioDialog must NOT be listed: MainWindow constructs it directly from app_gui globals, so app_gui-level class patches remain live and legitimate - the RenderWorker precedent. The dialog's QMediaPlayer/QAudioOutput fakes patch the_oracle.gui_recording by module object, never app_gui.

the_oracle.gui_cast.note: EXECUTED 2026-10-10 (the cast-bar cluster slice; the pre-flight below was recorded earlier the same day and is kept for the reasoning it carries). Only the row widget and the modal dialog are listed. _CastRow: the dialog builds its rows from gui_cast's globals, so an app_gui-level patch of it is a silent no-op. CastManagementDialog: listed as of this slice - its only app_gui runtime reader was the moved open_cast_manager (the __init__ use is an annotation), so no app_gui runtime reader remains, app_gui no longer re-exports it, and an app_gui-level patch of it is an offender to repoint at gui_cast (the _CastRow rule). SpeakerGroup, _speaker_settings_from_group and _apply_speaker_settings_to_group are NOT listed: a staying app_gui site reads each (SpeakerGroup - _build_ui builds panels A/B; _speaker_settings_from_group - _widget_snapshot; _apply_speaker_settings_to_group - _restore_speaker_section), so app_gui-level patches stay legitimate and the moved bodies receive them as INJECTIONS at the delegate boundary, resolved from app_gui's globals at call time. The four call-boundary names this slice injects are speaker_group_cls into _sync_extra_speaker_groups, settings_from_group_fn into _speaker_settings, and apply_settings_fn + normalize_keys_fn into apply_cast (the find_audiocpp_binary pattern) - normalize_cast_keys included (its staying readers are _load_project_into_ui and prepare_project, so it stays bare-resolvable at app_gui level and gains no PARTIAL_OWNED entry). A module-global read of any of the four inside gui_cast would turn every app_gui-level rebind of it into a silent no-op for the moved path; they stay unlistable permanently because their staying readers are window-assembly and persistence code that does not travel with the cluster. SpeakerSettings and speaker_config_from_payload need no seam: each is read at runtime only by the moved _speaker_config_from_payload body and each is already listed as moved-owned elsewhere in this record (the_oracle.models.settings; the_oracle.gui_settings), so app_gui-level patches are already offenders and the moved body resolves gui_cast's imports of them - and gui_cast joins payload_policy.policy_owners as a delegates owner for speaker_config_from_payload, since the decode delegate genuinely lives there now. SpeakerSettings' latent split adjudication is pruned in the same edit: app_gui keeps only annotation uses of it, so no runtime read remains on that side and the pair the latent net audits is gone. The ten cluster methods' bodies moved VERBATIM into gui_cast as main_window-taking functions (comments and blank lines preserved; the only textual edits are self -> main_window, the four injected names, and CastManagementDialog(self) -> CastManagementDialog(main_window)), and each app_gui method remains as a thin delegate whose body imports its owner function FUNCTION-LOCALLY (the settled entry-point delegate convention), so app_gui holds no module-level binding for any of them, an app_gui-level patch is a silent no-op, and gui_cast is the single patch point - literally what this listing records under rule 1.

the_oracle.gui_menu.note: extraction slice 12 (2026-10-10): the whole menu-bar body moved verbatim out of MainWindow._build_menu, which stays in app_gui as the thin call-site delegate (a method, so _build_menu itself is NOT listed here). `themes` crosses by injection at that boundary, so gui_menu binds no THEMES global and an app_gui-level THEMES rebind stays live for the moved body - the seam this slice is mutation-proven on. The patch-couple net needs no new bare-set exemption: neither QAction (imported by gui_menu) nor THEMES (injected) is in the suite's app_gui-rebind census. ENTRY-POINT DELEGATE CONVENTION (adjudicated 2026-10-10): the delegate imports build_menu FUNCTION-LOCALLY inside `_build_menu` (the slice-10 gui_ingest_tools style, settled as the campaign's single entry-point convention), so app_gui holds NO module-level binding for this name - an app_gui-level patch is a silent no-op and gui_menu is the single patch point, resolving at call time, which is what makes this listing literally true under rule 1. Before this, the module-level import made an app_gui-level patch LIVE for the delegate call while repointing at gui_menu was inert.

the_oracle.gui_ingest_tools.note: extraction slice 10 (2026-10-08): the ingest-tools handler flow bodies moved verbatim from MainWindow methods (which remain as thin delegates with the exact test-driven signatures); every patch-coupled Qt name crosses as an INJECTION parameter resolved from app_gui globals at call time (message_box_cls, file_dialog_cls) so app_gui-level wholesale rebinds keep intercepting the moved code

the_oracle.gui_tooltips.note: extraction slice 11 (2026-10-10): the Ctrl+hover description table moved verbatim from MainWindow._register_ctrl_help_descriptions (which remains a thin delegate with its exact call-site signature). The one patch-coupled name that body uses, cuda_reason, crosses as an INJECTION callable (cuda_reason_fn) resolved from app_gui globals at call time - the _vulkan_prerequisite_missing find_binary= precedent - so app_gui-level wholesale rebinds keep reaching the moved text, and this module needs no bare-set exemption (it binds no coupled name). ENTRY-POINT DELEGATE CONVENTION (adjudicated 2026-10-10): the delegate imports register_ctrl_help_descriptions FUNCTION-LOCALLY inside `_register_ctrl_help_descriptions` (the slice-10 gui_ingest_tools style, settled as the campaign's single entry-point convention), so app_gui holds NO module-level binding for this name - an app_gui-level patch is a silent no-op and gui_tooltips is the single patch point, resolving at call time, which is what makes this listing literally true under rule 1. Before this, the module-level import made an app_gui-level patch LIVE for the delegate call while repointing at gui_tooltips was inert.

payload_policy.description: Policy data for tests/test_payload_policy_ownership.py: which widgets feed the persisted settings payload, which read accessors count as 'reading a widget' for policy purposes, which MainWindow methods are sanctioned to read them outside the single-reader rule, where the payload policy functions may be referenced, and the schema keys whose hand-rolled copies outside gui_settings the net forbids. The net vacuity-guards this section (field floors) and cross-checks every payload_widgets entry against MainWindow.__init__'s assignments, so a stale or over-typed widget name fails here rather than blinding the reader scan.

writer_manifest.description: Policy data for tests/test_stem_cache_write_path.py's writer manifest: which write functions count as cache writes, which call/target shapes classify a write as stem- or preview-shaped, which source files are the gated owners of each kind, and the blindness floors under which the scan has demonstrably not gone blind. Stem writes must pass the engine-output gate (sanitize_engine_audio); preview writes are owned by OraclePipeline.render_preview (pause-only via _write_pause_only_stem, spoken via the gated engine path).

patch_couple_policy.description: Policy data for the patch-couple seam net (tests/test_app_gui_patch_surface.py): a name the suite rebinds at the app_gui module level is patch-coupled, and a moved gui_* module whose body resolves it as a bare global turns every app_gui-level rebind of it into a silent no-op. The net derives the coupled set from the test suite itself (self-updating census), scans every gui_* module's bare Name loads, and requires the raw bare set to equal the sanctioned exemptions EXACTLY: a new bare use fails until the call boundary injects the name (the 2ba2392 find_audiocpp_binary pattern) or the split is sanctioned here with a reason; a stale exemption fails until pruned. The same record also carries the LATENT split-readership adjudications: names no test rebinds YET but that both a staying app_gui function body and a gui_* module read in runtime position - the pair a future app_gui-level patch would silently half-cover. latent_split_readership entries are adjudicated with a reason and enforced with the same exact-set rule; latent_anchor_names and min_latent_pairs are the latent scan's blindness guards, mirroring the census's. The ANCHOR set is adjudicated alongside its pairs: THEMES left it on 2026-10-10 when tests/test_gui_menu_themes_seam.py rebinding app_gui.THEMES moved that name to the census side by construction - a name the census owns can never stay a LATENT anchor - and Path, read by eight gui_* modules' latent pairs, took its place so the guard stays three names strong.
